scrape_samples_scraped for each openstack-instance-exporter instance; used to spot unexpected metric/cardinality growth per hypervisor.

Source: Prometheus scrape metadata for the target(s) (up/scrape_* metrics).

panels.title: Exporter Scrape Samples per Scrape

scrape_duration_seconds{job="openstack-instance-exporter"}; time Prometheus spends scraping each exporter instance per hypervisor.

Source: Prometheus scrape metadata for the target(s) (up/scrape_* metrics).
Limitations: Reflects scrape health/latency and metric volume, not workload health. Network timeouts, relabeling, and Prometheus backpressure can affect values.
panels.title: Exporter Scrape Duration per Hypervisor

panels.description:
Wall-clock time for a full OIE background collection loop per hypervisor.

Source: OIE exporter instrumentation.
Limitations: This measures exporter work, not guest or application latency. Libvirt, conntrack, metadata, or local scheduling delays can increase the duration.
panels.title: Host Collection Cycle Duration

panels.description:
Elapsed time for OIE to read and process host conntrack state on each selected hypervisor.

Source: OIE's Linux kernel conntrack reader on the hypervisor.
Limitations: This measures exporter collection work, not guest or network latency. Large conntrack tables, kernel read delays, or exporter contention can increase the duration.
panels.title: Conntrack Collection Duration

panels.description:
Time spent listing domains and collecting Libvirt statistics in each OIE background collection cycle.

Source: OIE exporter instrumentation around the Libvirt domain collection.
Limitations: This measures exporter collection wall time, not guest or application latency; Libvirt responsiveness, domain count, and local scheduling delays can increase it.
panels.title: Libvirt Background Collector Duration

panels.description:
Time spent pruning stale entries from OIE's static and dynamic caches per hypervisor.

Source: OIE exporter instrumentation.
Limitations: This measures exporter housekeeping work, not guest or storage latency; cache size and local scheduling delays can increase the duration.
panels.title: Cache Cleanup Duration

panels.description:
increase(oie_host_collection_errors_total[$__rate_interval]); number of OIE background-collection errors on each hypervisor over the selected rate interval.

Source: OIE exporter instrumentation.
Limitations: This is a counter increase over the interval, not an errors-per-second rate. Exporter restart resets the counter, and this aggregate does not identify the failing collection stage by itself.
panels.title: Exporter Internal Collection Errors

Limitations: Measures exporter internals, not tenant workloads. Values reset on exporter restart; spikes can occur during large collections or scrapes.
panels.title: Exporter Process CPU Usage

panels.title: Exporter RSS (Resident Memory)

panels.title: Conntrack Raw Errors (Rate)

panels.description: Current source status per exporter target. A value of 1 means the most recent complete source collection succeeded; 0 means the source is unavailable or the exporter is serving retained last-good dependent data. Use the source-age panel to distinguish first-success unavailability from retained data after a failure. Prometheus up is a separate scrape-health signal.
panels.title: Conntrack and Libvirt Source Health

panels.description: Age of the last complete conntrack and Libvirt collections. A value of -1 means that source has never completed successfully. When source health is 0 and age is non-negative, dependent metrics may be retained last-good values; they are observable but not fresh and bundled workload alerts are freshness-gated.
panels.title: Conntrack and Libvirt Last-Success Age

panels.description: Counts resource axes by current data state for the selected instance/project scope. Fresh means available=1 and fresh=1. Root/boot volumes are included when Libvirt exposes a matching job; their retype support and outcome still depend on the OpenStack and storage path. Source RBD Pool and Destination RBD Pool are parsed from the saved RBD image names; they are not Cinder volume-type names. Source RBD Image and Destination RBD Image are RBD image basenames that retain the volume- prefix; strip that prefix before passing either value to openstack volume show. Once a job is known, the completion-paced fast poller inspects mirror XML no more often than every 5 seconds, with the interval beginning after the preceding attempt completes. Block-job progress is queried no more often than every 15 seconds after the preceding query completes and waits 30 seconds after a failed query completes before retrying. Initial discovery remains bounded to 256 domain XML reads per exporter collection cycle and still runs during normal collections when no retype is known; only the idle fast-poller and block-job paths make no Libvirt calls. All lifecycle fields for one retained operation are merged into one table row. If the exact same source/destination identity is observed repeatedly on one instance disk, only its newest retained row is kept. Status 1 means copying is in progress. Status 5 means Libvirt reports the copy ready and awaiting pivot; this is non-terminal and does not prove Cinder success. Status 6 means that copy-ready state has remained for at least 10 minutes since this exporter first observed it and requires operator attention. Status 2 means a successful terminal XML inspection found the destination as the live source. Status 3 means that inspection found the original source, which can represent a failed or cancelled operation. Status 4 is emitted only when a successful XML inspection finds the mirror gone but cannot match the final live source to the saved source or destination. A job that merely becomes too old to reconfirm expires without a terminal status, row, timestamp, or result-counter increment. Libvirt Observation is Healthy when the latest block-job information query succeeded and Unavailable when that query failed; the per-job observation and progress fields are omitted while the main Libvirt source is unavailable; it is not a statement about the Nova or Cinder outcome. Libvirt Job Present remains Yes for copying, copy-ready, and ready-stalled jobs until the job is pivoted or aborted. First Observed, Copy Ready Observed, and Terminal Observed are exporter observation timestamps, not authoritative Cinder API lifecycle timestamps. Recent rows, timestamps, and result counters are in-memory exporter-process state and reset on exporter restart. A terminal row is retained for one hour, with at most 256 retained rows per exporter, and then disappears; Prometheus historical retention remains independent. Logical progress is Libvirt/QEMU's approximate cur/end position across the block job's logical work range, not Ceph physical allocation, transferred bytes, or an ETA. Thin-provisioned or sparse regions and regions discarded by guest fstrim/TRIM, when discard propagated to RBD, can require little or no data transfer, so progress is not time-linear and retyping can finish sooner than percentage extrapolation suggests. Progress is omitted when Libvirt has no usable current total or the latest query failed, except that copy-ready XML independently proves the logical copy phase reached 100%. An empty table can mean no matching observations or unavailable telemetry; check the visible coverage indicators.

panels.description:
Diagnostic only: a write near the end of a sparse image can produce a large highest-written offset while little data is stored. Neither the offset nor its ratio to capacity is a usage measurement, for RBD or file-backed images.

Sum of guest-visible logical disk capacity and Libvirt's highest-written offset for attached instance disks. Both lines use the same cohort: only disks for which Libvirt supplies both fields. This is a virtual disk address-space view, not a storage-utilization view.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU block stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Libvirt block allocation is the offset of the highest written sector, not the number of bytes physically allocated. For Ceph RBD it does not measure allocated RADOS objects, shared clone/snapshot data, replication or erasure-coding overhead, compression, or backend reclamation after discard/TRIM. Missing Libvirt allocation fields are omitted rather than replaced with physical/container size. Use Ceph-native telemetry for authoritative backend consumption.
